description: The National Emergency Management Organisation of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines publishes the volcanic hazard map of St. Vincent as an image with a description of its four zones. Zone 1 (red, very high hazard) is the area of expected total destruction from pyroclastic flows, surges and mudflows and maximum damage from projectiles, likely to receive more than 30 cm of ash and unsuitable for habitation during an eruption. Zone 2 (orange, high hazard) covers moderate flow and surge hazard, the 5 km projectile zone and 10 to 30 cm of ash. Zone 3 (yellow, moderate hazard) is free of flows and surges but gets 5 to 10 cm of ash, minor earthquakes and lightning. Zone 4 (green, low hazard) gets less than 5 cm of ash, where crop damage and disruption of water supply are the main effects. The page notes that the map shows zones on land only, although lahars and pyroclastic hazards also reach offshore. Access is free on the web; no licence is stated. Caveats: the map is a single image, not GIS data, and its date and authors are not given on the page read. Coverage is St. Vincent. It supports exposure analysis of roads, water supply and settlements to volcanic hazards; related records are VMGD volcanic alert levels and the IMO Reykjanes volcanic hazard map.
